title: Income Tax Rates Amendment (Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015
short_title: Income Tax Rates Amendment (Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would set income tax rates for specified managed investment trust liabilities as part of the proposed new taxation system for these trusts.
It would apply top marginal rates to certain income allocation shortfalls and set rates for trustee tax on amounts attributed to foreign residents.
The bill would support the main trust reform legislation alongside separate bills dealing with Medicare levy treatment and tax imposed on excess tax offsets.
changes: Trustee tax on non-arm’s length income would be set at 30 per cent.
Amounts attributed to foreign resident companies under the relevant trustee liability provision would attract the standard corporate rate.
Other specified foreign resident allocations would use rates for a single foreign resident individual or the highest foreign resident individual marginal rate.
summary.affected: Managed investment trust trustees would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Income Tax Rates Amendment (Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015 sets the trustee tax rate for unattributed income at the highest individual marginal rate plus the Medicare levy, ensuring that income not attributed to investors does not escape taxation.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The bills create a new tax system for eligible managed investment trusts, reducing compliance costs by $30 million per year and taxing investors directly, modernising rules for Australia’s $2.6 trillion funds management industry.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: A motion was moved requesting the Senate to resume consideration of 14 specified bills from the previous session, with each request to be conveyed in a separate message. The bills covered water amendment, managed investment trusts, social services, crime commission, deaths registration, tax and superannuation, crowd-sourced funding, firearms trafficking, and parliamentary entitlements.
